files.filename: Work Order and Change Order Process.docx
files.search:
Loblolly Ridge Therapeutics • 1.3
Work Order and Change Order Process
Loblolly Ridge Therapeutics | Outsourcing & Procurement with Finance and 
Legal | 2026-03-02 | v1.3
How a scope of work becomes a signed work order or change order at Loblolly Ridge: who 
asks, who prices, who checks, who approves at which value, and what is filed before work 
starts. Owned by Outsourcing & Procurement with Finance and Legal. Version 1.3.
When this process applies
Use it for every new work order with a qualified partner, every change order that adds 
scope, time or money, and every SOW amendment that changes rates or timelines. 
Purchases of goods and catalog services go through purchase orders in the finance system 
instead.
What the requester provides
 A scope request from the program owner: objective, deliverables, timeline and the 
project and budget line it will be charged to.
 For clinical work, the estimated pass-through costs (site fees, investigator payments, 
patient reimbursement) as well as services.
 For GxP work, confirmation from QA that the partner is qualified and a quality 
agreement is in place.
Roles
 Program owner – writes the scope, reviews the partner's proposal, confirms the work is 
needed.
 Outsourcing & Procurement – checks rates against the master agreement and 
benchmarks, tightens scope and negotiates.
 Finance – checks the amount against the approved budget and the reforecast, and sets 
up the accrual method.
 Legal – reviews terms and the transfer of obligations for clinical work.
 Approver – signs at the level set by the total value.
Approval thresholds
Approval is set by the total value including estimated pass-through, not by the services 
value alone: directors up to $250,000; CFO from $250,000 to $1 million; CEO from $1 
million to $5 million; board $5 million or more.
Loblolly Ridge Therapeutics • 1.3
Separately, any commitment of $5 million or more that is not in the approved budget needs 
board approval under the stage-gate procedure.
Steps and handoffs
1. Program owner submits the scope request to Outsourcing & Procurement.
2. The partner prices the scope.
3. Outsourcing & Procurement reviews rates and scope and returns questions to the 
partner.
4. Finance confirms budget cover or flags the variance for the reforecast.
5. Legal reviews the document.
6. The approver signs at the threshold level; the partner countersigns.
7. Outsourcing & Procurement files the signed document in the contract repository and 
updates the work order register before work starts.
Exceptions
Urgent scope may start under a written authorization for up to 30 days and $100,000 while 
the change order is completed. Retroactive change orders, where work started without a 
signed document or authorization, need CFO sign-off and are reported to the Portfolio 
Review Committee.
Outputs and records
A signed work order or change order in the contract repository; an updated line in the work 
order register with committed services, estimated pass-through, status and approval level; 
and an accrual method set in the finance system: activity reports and milestones for CRO 
services, CRO visit estimates for pass-through, percentage of completion for GLP studies, 
batch stage for CDMOs, straight-line for fixed fees.
Deliverables named in the work order are logged on receipt and reviewed by QA, the 
technical owner or Finance depending on type. The roles above are set out in more detail in 
the RACI appendix.
Changes in version 1.3
Thresholds restated to include estimated pass-through; the 30-day urgent authorization 
limit added; retroactive change orders now reported to the Portfolio Review Committee.

files.title: LRT-4051 Phase 1 Outsourcing Options
files.search:
LRT-4051 Phase 1 Outsourcing Options
Sourcing options for the first-in-human study of LRT-4051, for discussion with the Chief 
Development Officer and the CFO on August 20, 2026. No vendor is being selected today.
Loblolly Ridge Therapeutics | Clinical Operations with Outsourcing | 2026-08-20 | 1
Decision requested
Agree which sourcing models go into the request for proposal planned for November and 
December 2026, and agree the evaluation criteria. No vendor choice and no budget commitment 
are requested today; no first-in-human sourcing decision has been made.
Loblolly Ridge Therapeutics | Clinical Operations with Outsourcing | 2026-08-20 | 2
Why decide the model now
LRT-4051 is an investigational oral small molecule for diabetic kidney disease, nominated at G2 in 
September 2025. The FY2026 plan has the IND submitted on April 30, 2027. GLP repeat-dose in-
life phases finished in late July, about two weeks after plan. The first-in-human study will be 
outsourced: we have no clinical pharmacology unit and no in-house data management.
Loblolly Ridge Therapeutics | Clinical Operations with Outsourcing | 2026-08-20 | 3
Option A – full-service CRO
One partner runs the unit relationship, data management, biostatistics, safety reporting support 
and medical writing. This is closest to how CANOPY-1 works: Halvorsen performs site activation, 
monitoring, data management, the eTMF and pass-through payments, while we keep the 
protocol, medical monitoring oversight, safety reporting decisions and regulatory submissions. 
Least coordination for our team; least control over unit choice.
Loblolly Ridge Therapeutics | Clinical Operations with Outsourcing | 2026-08-20 | 4
Option B – Phase 1 unit plus functional vendors
Contract a clinical pharmacology unit directly and add separate vendors for data management and 
biostatistics. Merrow Clinical Pharmacology Unit is completing a feasibility assessment. Gives us 
the most say over the unit, dosing schedule and data standards; needs more sponsor coordination 
and three contracts instead of one.
Loblolly Ridge Therapeutics | Clinical Operations with Outsourcing | 2026-08-20 | 5
Option C – extend an existing CRO relationship
Add the study to an existing master agreement with a qualified CRO, which would place the unit 
as a subcontractor. Fastest contracting route and a known team; the unit would be one step 
removed, so we would oversee a subcontracted activity.
Loblolly Ridge Therapeutics | Clinical Operations with Outsourcing | 2026-08-20 | 6
Evaluation criteria
Unit availability for a start after the IND is in effect.
 Sponsor oversight load on Clinical Operations in 2027, while CANOPY-1 runs to database lock.
 Fit with our data standards and transfer checks.
 Qualification: tier 1 partners need QA approval and a quality agreement before a work order.
 Cost and contracting time; approval level depends on total value, including pass-through.
Loblolly Ridge Therapeutics | Clinical Operations with Outsourcing | 2026-08-20 | 7
Preliminary assessment
Options B and C look stronger than A on control and speed, but the evidence is thin. Cost is 
compared qualitatively here; the pricing benchmark mentioned in July was not circulated with this 
deck. No option is recommended yet.
Loblolly Ridge Therapeutics | Clinical Operations with Outsourcing | 2026-08-20 | 8
Information still needed
Merrow feasibility assessment and QA qualification outcome.
 Confirmed IND timing once GLP report dates are firm.
 Clinical Operations capacity plan for 2027.
 Our GLP bioanalysis partners' ability to support clinical PK: Alder Bioanalytical and Kestrel DMPK 
Services are already on the IND-enabling program.
Loblolly Ridge Therapeutics | Clinical Operations with Outsourcing | 2026-08-20 | 9
Timeline to request for proposal
August to October – feasibility, requirements and short list of models.
 November to December – request for proposal to shortlisted partners.
 First quarter 2027 – selection, qualification close-out and contracting at the approval level the 
value requires.
Loblolly Ridge Therapeutics | Clinical Operations with Outsourcing | 2026-08-20 | 10

files.title: CANOPY-1 CRO Oversight Plan
files.search:
Loblolly Ridge Therapeutics • 2.1
CANOPY-1 CRO Oversight Plan
Loblolly Ridge Therapeutics | Clinical Operations | 2026-04-30 | v2.1
This plan sets out how Loblolly Ridge oversees Halvorsen Clinical Research and the other 
service providers on CANOPY-1. It records which obligations have been transferred, what 
the sponsor keeps, how each area is overseen, which indicators are tracked and how issues 
are escalated. Version 2.1 adds the CANOPY-OLE work order and the recruitment vendor.
1. Study and partners
CANOPY-1 is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled pivotal study planned to 
randomize 640 adults with treatment-resistant hypertension at 112 sites in 11 countries. 
After a 12-week double-blind period, participants may enter the CANOPY-OLE extension.
Halvorsen Clinical Research is the full-service CRO under a master work order effective June 
1, 2024, and for CANOPY-OLE under a separate work order effective April 20, 2026. Other 
partners are Meridian Central Laboratories (central lab), Cobalt RTSM (IRT), Pulsewell 
ABPM Services (ambulatory blood-pressure monitoring), Harbor Safety Services (safety 
database), Clearwing Clinical Supply (packaging and depots), Alder Bioanalytical (PK 
samples) and, since March 2026, Siteline Recruitment Services.
2. Transfer of obligations
Under 21 CFR 312.52 a transfer of sponsor obligations to a CRO must be described in 
writing, and anything not described stays with the sponsor. The CANOPY-1 transfer of 
obligations, attached to the master work order, transfers site selection and activation, 
monitoring, data management, the eTMF and pass-through payments to Halvorsen.
Loblolly Ridge retains the protocol, medical monitoring oversight, safety reporting 
decisions, approval of the statistical analysis plan, regulatory submissions and final 
acceptance of the trial master file. As ICH E6(R3) puts it, the sponsor keeps ultimate 
responsibility for transferred activities.
Loblolly Ridge Therapeutics • 2.1
3. Sponsor study team
The Loblolly Ridge study team has 12 people in clinical operations, 3 in biometrics, 2 
medical monitors and a program lead. Each oversight area below has a named sponsor 
owner in the study contact list.
4. Oversight by area
 Monitoring: sponsor review of monitoring visit reports and central monitoring outputs. 
Centralized monitoring is a systematic analytical evaluation of study conduct across 
sites; Halvorsen runs it and the sponsor reviews the signals monthly.
 Data: blinded EDC extracts arrive monthly, IRT extracts weekly, central lab and 
ambulatory blood-pressure data on schedule; Biometrics checks each transfer on 
receipt.
 Trial master file: quarterly completeness checks of the eTMF, the sponsor's repository 
of essential trial records, with final acceptance by the sponsor at close.
 Safety: medical monitors review serious adverse event reports and decide on expedited 
reporting; Harbor Safety Services hosts the safety database.
 Supply: IRT supply alerts and depot stock reviewed with Clinical Supply every week.
 Finance: pass-through spend and activity reports reviewed monthly for the accrual.
Loblolly Ridge Therapeutics • 2.1
5. Subcontracted activities
Halvorsen subcontracts some country start-up and translation work. ICH E6(R3) expects 
the sponsor to oversee important transferred activities, including those a provider 
subcontracts, and to have access to providers' SOPs and performance metrics.
Halvorsen notifies the sponsor before adding or replacing a subcontractor, and its 
subcontractors are listed in the quarterly business review pack.
6. Key performance indicators
The indicators and thresholds are set out below. The calculation rules for each indicator are 
in Appendix B, the KPI calculation sheet.
 Site activations against the activation plan.
 Randomizations against the current forecast.
 Monitoring visit reports finalized within 10 business days of the visit.
 Queries open more than 30 days: below 5% of open queries.
 Important protocol deviations reviewed within 5 business days.
 eTMF completeness at least 90% at each quarterly check.
 Activity reports for accrual received by working day 3.
7. Governance and escalation
Sponsor and CRO hold a monthly joint operations committee and a bimonthly business 
review. An issue that is unresolved after two meetings escalates to the Senior Director, 
Clinical Operations and Halvorsen's executive sponsor. Decisions and actions are minuted 
by Halvorsen and approved by the sponsor within five business days.
8. Records
Oversight evidence is filed in the sponsor section of the trial master file: joint operations 
committee minutes, business review packs, KPI reports, transfer check logs, eTMF check 
results and escalation records.

CANOPY-1 Enrollment Forecast Working Session with Halvorsen
Working session between the Loblolly Ridge CANOPY-1 study team and Halvorsen project 
leadership, June 18, 2026. Purpose: agree a planning assumption for last participant randomized 
after slower-than-planned site activation in two countries. Data are from the May 31 cut.
Loblolly Ridge Therapeutics | Clinical Operations | 2026-06-18 | 1
Where we are at May 31
383 participants randomized (60% of the 640 target) from 827 screened, with 98 of 112 planned 
sites active. The baseline plan called for 438 randomized by this date. Randomizations were 19 in 
March, 33 in April and 27 in May.
Loblolly Ridge Therapeutics | Clinical Operations | 2026-06-18 | 2
What the plan assumed
The FY2026 baseline has last participant randomized on December 31, 2026, database lock on 
June 4, 2027 and topline results on July 2, 2027. The study runs in 11 countries: the United States, 
Canada, Mexico, Argentina, Poland, Hungary, the Czech Republic, Spain, Germany, Bulgaria and 
Romania.
Loblolly Ridge Therapeutics | Clinical Operations | 2026-06-18 | 3
The gap is concentrated in two countries
Site activation in Argentina and Germany has been slower than planned. The study team's current 
view is that regulatory and ethics start-up timelines in those two countries are the main cause.
Loblolly Ridge Therapeutics | Clinical Operations | 2026-06-18 | 4
Questions for Halvorsen
Which remaining sites in Argentina and Germany have submission dates, and which are waiting 
on documents?
 What start-up resource is assigned to each late country, and has it changed this year?

files.title: LRT-1107 Development Program Overview
files.search:
Loblolly Ridge Therapeutics • 3.0
LRT-1107 Development Program 
Overview
Loblolly Ridge Therapeutics | Clinical Development | 2026-09-21 | v3.0
LRT-1107 is an investigational oral small molecule in Phase 3 development for treatment-
resistant hypertension. It is not approved for any use, and this overview makes no 
statement about its effects. It describes the program's objective, its studies, the regulatory 
interactions to date, manufacturing and supply readiness, the timeline to topline results and 
the questions still open. Version 3.0 replaces the June 2026 edition. A shorter version is 
available for prospective ex-U.S. partners under a confidentiality agreement.
Program objective and status
The objective is a registration package for LRT-1107 in adults whose blood pressure 
remains uncontrolled despite multiple antihypertensive medicines. The program completed 
its end-of-phase-2 meeting with FDA in February 2024, and the Portfolio Review Committee 
recommended, and the board approved, the Phase 3 gate (G5) in April 2024.
Loblolly Ridge holds all rights. The company is open to partners for ex-U.S. rights to 
LRT-1107; an early commercial assessment by Harrowgate Insights was completed in 
September 2026, and its findings are not part of this overview.
Study portfolio
CANOPY-1 is the pivotal study: randomized, double-blind and placebo-controlled, planned 
to randomize 640 adults at 112 sites in 11 countries (the United States, Canada, Mexico, 
Argentina, Poland, Hungary, the Czech Republic, Spain, Germany, Bulgaria and Romania). 
After a 12-week double-blind period, participants may enter CANOPY-OLE, the open-label 
extension, which enrolled its first participant on June 11, 2026.
By August 31, 2026, CANOPY-1 had screened 1,005 and randomized 467 participants, 73% 
of target, with 104 of the 112 planned sites active. The chart shows randomizations by 
month. Earlier clinical pharmacology and Phase 2 studies are summarized in the 
investigator's brochure.

Loblolly Ridge Therapeutics • 3.0
How the studies are run
Halvorsen Clinical Research is the full-service CRO for CANOPY-1 under a master work 
order effective June 1, 2024, and for CANOPY-OLE under a work order effective April 20, 
2026.
Halvorsen performs site selection and activation, monitoring, data management, the eTMF 
and pass-through payments. Loblolly Ridge retains the protocol, medical monitoring 
oversight, safety reporting decisions, statistical analysis plan approval, regulatory 
submissions and final acceptance of the trial master file.
Other study partners are Meridian Central Laboratories, Cobalt RTSM, Pulsewell ABPM 
Services, Harbor Safety Services, Clearwing Clinical Supply, Alder Bioanalytical and, since 
March 2026, Siteline Recruitment Services. An independent DSMB, supported by 
Harborview DSMB Services, met in October 2025 and April 2026; its next review is on 
October 14, 2026.
Regulatory interactions
The end-of-phase-2 meeting in February 2024 is the most recent formal meeting with FDA 
on the program. The next planned interaction is a pre-NDA meeting request, now forecast 
for December 2027 after topline results. Regulatory correspondence is held by Regulatory 
Affairs and is not reproduced here.
Manufacturing and clinical supply
LRT-1107 drug substance (API) is made by Tessaro Fine Chemicals in Italy and drug 
product by Northgate Pharma Services in Ontario. Clearwing Clinical Supply packages, 
labels and distributes to depots in the United States and the Netherlands. Loblolly Ridge 
keeps at least six months of forecast drug-product demand as safety stock across the two 
depots, and no site has run out of study drug.
Tessaro is the only qualified API source. Hanlin Pharmatech in China is being qualified as a 
backup API supplier; its qualification audit took place on June 9, 2026, the audit response 
has not yet been accepted, and the qualification batch is forecast for February 2027.
Timeline to topline
The current forecast is last participant randomized March 16, 2027, last participant last 
visit July 6, 2027, database lock August 17, 2027 and topline results September 14, 2027. 
The FY2026 baseline had last participant randomized on December 31, 2026 and topline on 
July 2, 2027.
To protect the forecast, change order 4 would add one country with six planned sites and 
about three months of CRO services, valued at $3.72 million in services plus an estimated 
$2.38 million in pass-through. It needs board approval at the October 8, 2026 meeting.
Loblolly Ridge Therapeutics • 3.0
Open questions
 Whether randomization recovers enough in the autumn to hold the March 2027 
forecast, with or without the added country.
 Timing of backup API approval relative to the drug-product campaigns needed after 
2027.
 Scope and timing of any ex-U.S. partnership, which the company would discuss before 
topline under a confidentiality agreement.
 Size of pharmacokinetic sampling in CANOPY-OLE, which affects 2027 bioanalytical 
capacity.

files.search:
LRT-2240 Non-Confidential Partnering Presentation
LRT-2240: an investigational oral small molecule for chemotherapy-induced peripheral 
neuropathy. Non-confidential overview for prospective partners, May 2026. LRT-2240 is not 
approved for any use.
Loblolly Ridge Therapeutics | Business Development | 2026-05-12 | 1
The problem a partner would take on
Chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy is a common and often dose-limiting side effect of 
several widely used chemotherapy classes. Treatment options are limited, and oncologists 
sometimes reduce or stop chemotherapy because of it. We are looking for a partner to take an 
oral option through later-stage development.
Loblolly Ridge Therapeutics | Business Development | 2026-05-12 | 2
LRT-2240 at a glance
Investigational oral small molecule.
 In-licensed from Tamsin Biosciences in 2019; Loblolly Ridge holds exclusive worldwide 
development and commercialization rights.
 Study 2240-201, a Phase 2a study, completed its last participant visit in November 2025; the 
clinical study report is being finalized.
 Clinical, nonclinical and CMC information is available under a confidentiality agreement.
Loblolly Ridge Therapeutics | Business Development | 2026-05-12 | 3
Proposed development path
The proposed next step is a Phase 2b study. Its design is being drafted with input from our clinical 
and regulatory teams and will be shared with partners under a confidentiality agreement, 
together with the Phase 2a data and the CMC plan.
Loblolly Ridge Therapeutics | Business Development | 2026-05-12 | 4
Partnership structures we would consider
A global license.
 A regional license.
 A co-development arrangement.
 In each case Loblolly Ridge would keep an option to co-promote in the United States.
Loblolly Ridge Therapeutics | Business Development | 2026-05-12 | 5
About Loblolly Ridge
Loblolly Ridge Therapeutics is a clinical-stage company in The Woodlands, Texas, developing oral 
small-molecule medicines for serious chronic cardiometabolic, renal and neuropathic-pain 
conditions. We combine in-house discovery biology, DMPK, clinical development, regulatory and 
quality teams with a qualified network of clinical, nonclinical and manufacturing partners.
Loblolly Ridge Therapeutics | Business Development | 2026-05-12 | 6
Next conversation
If LRT-2240 fits your portfolio, we will put a confidentiality agreement in place and open the data 
room, followed by a scientific and clinical discussion with our team. Please contact Business 
Development at Loblolly Ridge Therapeutics.
Loblolly Ridge Therapeutics | Business Development | 2026-05-12 | 7

files.search:
Loblolly Ridge Therapeutics • 1.0
LRT-3318 Technology Transfer Status 
Note
Loblolly Ridge Therapeutics | CMC & Clinical Supply | 2026-09-14 | v1.0
Status of the LRT-3318 drug-substance technology transfer from Loblolly Ridge to 
Castellane Pharma, as of September 14, 2026. Prepared by CMC & Clinical Supply for the 
Castellane technical team, the internal CMC team and the alliance manager, and shared with 
Castellane ahead of the October joint steering committee.
Scope of the transfer
Castellane runs all development, regulatory and commercial activities for LRT-3318, 
including its ongoing Phase 1b study. Loblolly Ridge supplies drug substance at a transfer 
price until technology transfer to Castellane's manufacturer completes, targeted for March 
2027.
The transfer covers seven packages: analytical methods, reference standards, process 
description, batch history, stability and specifications, impurity control, and regulatory CMC 
module support. Tessaro Fine Chemicals, which makes LRT-3318 drug substance for 
Loblolly Ridge, supports the process and batch-history packages. The diagram shows how 
knowledge and material move between the parties.
Package status
 Analytical methods – accepted April 22 (due April 30).
 Reference standards – accepted April 24 (due April 30).
Loblolly Ridge Therapeutics • 1.0
 Process description – accepted July 9 (due June 30).
 Batch history – accepted August 27 (due August 31).
 Stability and specifications – accepted September 11 (due August 31).
 Impurity control – due October 30; at risk. Castellane has asked for additional purge 
data.
 Regulatory CMC module support – due January 29, 2027; on schedule.
Supply obligations and deliveries
Drug substance deliveries to Castellane were 6.0 kg on February 24 and 8.5 kg on June 23, 
2026. The next delivery, 8.5 kg, is scheduled for November 20, 2026, with further deliveries 
planned for March and June 2027 while Castellane's manufacturer qualifies.
In the alliance obligations tracker at the August 31 cut, 4 of the 7 packages had been 
accepted and 14.5 kg had been delivered in two shipments.
Open technical items
 Impurity purge data: CMC & Clinical Supply to compile existing purge and spiking 
results by September 30 and agree with Castellane whether new experiments are 
needed. Owner: Dr. Ingrid Solberg.
 Regulatory CMC module support: Castellane to confirm the module sections it needs 
from Loblolly Ridge. Owner: Castellane regulatory CMC lead.
 November delivery: release testing plan confirmed with Tessaro. Owner: CMC & Clinical 
Supply.
Change control during transfer
Until the transfer completes, any change to the process, specifications or analytical methods 
is agreed by both parties before it is made. ICH Q10 notes that change-management 
formality generally differs before and after the initial regulatory submission, so the parties 
will revisit the change-control arrangement when Castellane files its own manufacturing 
information.
Governance and planned completion
Items are reviewed at the joint development committee and escalated to the quarterly joint 
steering committee; Chloe Tran is the Loblolly Ridge alliance manager. Technology transfer 
completion remains targeted for March 2027, and depends on closing the impurity control 
package.

files.title: LRT-4051 IND-Enabling Development Plan
files.search:
Loblolly Ridge Therapeutics • 1.3
LRT-4051 IND-Enabling Development 
Plan
Loblolly Ridge Therapeutics | LRT-4051 Program Team | 2026-09-04 | v1.3
LRT-4051 is an investigational oral small molecule for diabetic kidney disease, nominated 
as a development candidate at gate G2 in September 2025. This plan sets the target date for 
its IND, the IND-enabling workstreams in dependency order, the partners doing the work, 
the regulatory interaction plan, the risks to the timeline and what the G3 decision will need. 
Version 1.3 updates the forecast after the August schedule review.
Target: IND submission June 4, 2027
The FY2026 plan baseline was April 30, 2027. The forecast is now June 4, 2027, because 
GLP toxicology final reports are forecast for December 4, 2026 (baseline October 30) and 
GMP API release for December 11, 2026 (baseline October 16). Both sit on the critical path. 
The IND-enabling workplan has 44 tasks: 13 complete, 10 in progress and 21 not started, 
with 18 on the critical path.
Workstreams in dependency order
Nonclinical safety. GLP repeat-dose toxicology in two species drives the plan. The in-life 
phases finished in late July, about two weeks after plan; draft reports follow, then an 
internal QA audit of the drafts, then final reports. ICH M3(R2) links the duration of 
repeated-dose toxicity studies to the duration and scope of the planned clinical trials, so the 
study durations were set for the planned first-in-human study. The genetic toxicology 
battery is complete and the safety pharmacology core battery is due in October.
DMPK. Toxicokinetic sample analysis feeds the human dose projection memo, which the 
first-in-human synopsis and the nonclinical summaries both need. Metabolite profiling in 
the toxicology species runs in parallel.
CMC. The GMP API campaign is followed by release testing and a certificate of analysis, then 
clinical drug product manufacture and release. The API stability program starts after 
release.
Regulatory writing. Nonclinical written and tabulated summaries start when the final 
toxicology reports arrive; the quality module and investigator's brochure run alongside; 
IND assembly and publishing follow.
Loblolly Ridge Therapeutics • 1.3
Who does the work
Quarry Hill Preclinical runs GLP toxicology and safety pharmacology, Ashcombe Genetic 
Toxicology the genetic toxicology battery, Alder Bioanalytical GLP bioanalysis and Kestrel 
DMPK Services non-GLP pharmacokinetics. Tessaro Fine Chemicals makes GMP API and 
Northgate Pharma Services drug product; Brookmoor Analytical does analytical and 
stability work. Inkwell Medical Writing and Parkway Regulatory Publishing support the IND 
documents. Each GLP testing facility has a quality assurance unit independent of the study 
staff, which our qualification confirms, and our QA audits the draft toxicology reports.
Regulatory interaction plan
We will request a pre-IND meeting with FDA, now forecast for November 20, 2026, with the 
meeting expected in February 2027. The briefing package will cover the nonclinical 
program, the CMC approach and the first-in-human design. Advice from the meeting will be 
reflected in the IND and in the final first-in-human protocol.
Risks to the timeline
Toxicology reporting is the main risk. Any further delay in draft reports moves the QA audit, 
the final reports and the nonclinical summaries day for day.
API release depends on the campaign at Tessaro and release testing at Brookmoor; the 
genotoxic impurity method must be ready before release testing.
First-in-human sourcing has not been decided, and the request for proposal planned for 
November and December could run into January. This affects study start, not the IND date.
The regulatory team also supports the LRT-1107 program in 2027, so writing capacity will 
be tight in the first half of the year. Study titles and report numbers for all IND-enabling 
studies are listed in Appendix A.
The G3 decision
The G3 decision to submit the IND is planned for April 2027 and will be made by the CEO on 
the Portfolio Review Committee's recommendation. Gate G3 asks whether the IND package 
is complete and the first clinical study is ready to place. The gate package will show the 
complete nonclinical and CMC evidence, the pre-IND outcome, the first-in-human plan and 
sourcing decision, and the 2027 budget and FTE request. Under the stage-gate procedure 
the CEO approves G0 to G3 decisions within budget.

files.search:
Research Laboratory Operations Guide
Loblolly Ridge Therapeutics | Facilities, Lab Operations & EHS | 2026-03-16
How the Woodlands research laboratory runs day to day: its areas, how to book instruments, how
maintenance and calibration are handled, where samples live, the safety basics and who to call.
Read it in your first week and keep it handy. Rev. C, March 2026.
The laboratory at a glance
The laboratory occupies 17,500 square feet in the same building as our offices in The Woodlands. It
has five areas: bioanalytical and analytical, cell biology, assay development, chemistry support and
shared equipment. About 20 instruments are booked through the instrument calendar; the rest are
open use or assigned to a team.
Research at the Woodlands laboratory is non-GxP. We still keep research records attributable,
contemporaneous and reviewed, because the data feed decisions and may later support regulatory
documents. GLP work is done only at qualified external testing facilities.
Booking instruments
Book bookable instruments in the instrument calendar in 30-minute blocks, up to four weeks ahead.
Cancel at least 24 hours ahead so someone else can use the slot.
The two LC-MS/MS triple-quadrupole systems also run an unattended overnight queue, giving
about 100 available hours a week each. Load overnight batches through the DMPK queue, not the
calendar.
If an instrument is faulty, mark the booking and tell Lab Operations the same day; do not attempt
repairs yourself.
Maintenance and calibration
Service vendors carry out preventive maintenance every 6 to 12 months depending on instrument
type. Lab Operations schedules the visits and books the instrument out in the calendar.
Maintenance and calibration records are kept in the Lab Operations spreadsheet and in the
vendors' portals. Check the calibration label before using a balance or pipette; if it is past due, use
another and tell Lab Operations.
Samples, freezers and inventory
Register every sample in the assay and sample registry before it goes into storage, and label it with
the registry ID. Freezer positions are recorded on the freezer map on the Lab Operations share. Do
not store food or personal items in any laboratory freezer or refrigerator. Chemicals are received
and logged by Lab Operations into the chemical inventory before use.

Safety basics
Complete laboratory safety training before starting work, and refresher training every year.
Wear a lab coat, safety glasses and gloves in all laboratory areas.
Biohazard waste goes in the red bins; Lab Operations arranges pickup.
Freezer alarms page the on-call Lab Operations staff member. If you hear an alarm out of hours
and no one has responded, call the on-call number posted at each freezer bank.
Report every spill, injury or near miss to Lab Operations the same day.
Contacts
Lab Operations & EHS (bookings, maintenance, freezers, waste, training): Beth Kowalczyk,
Manager, Lab Operations & EHS.
LC-MS/MS queue and bioanalytical methods: DMPK & Bioanalytical, Dr. Mateo Arriaga.
ELN, assay registry and data hub access: Research Informatics, Samuel Oyelaran.
Instrument computers and network: IT, Tyler Brandon.

Instrument register with maintenance data and weekly available, booked, used and down hours for 20 bookable instruments.
See each dataset dictionary and summary. Missing numeric values are excluded, not zero.
Descriptive statistics of selected records only. Totals of percentages and adjustment values are not operating KPIs.

Register of the 68 laboratory instruments and weekly utilization of the 20 bookable instruments from March 2 to August 28, 2026. Prepared by Lab Operations to support the bioanalytical capacity review.
Data 1 – instrument register: type, laboratory area, bookable flag, installation date, last preventive maintenance, maintenance interval, service vendor and status for all 68 instruments.
Data 2 – instrument-week utilization: 520 records, one per bookable instrument per week, with capacity, available, booked, used and downtime hours and the number of runs.

Available hours: scheduled hours the instrument could run in the week. For each of the two LC-MS/MS triple-quadrupole systems this includes the unattended overnight queue, about 100 hours a week; holiday weeks are lower.
Downtime hours: recorded breakdown, repair and maintenance time.
Capacity hours: available hours minus downtime. Utilization is measured against capacity hours.
Booked hours: hours reserved in the instrument calendar or the overnight queue.
Used hours: hours with a run logged on the instrument.

Utilization is not precomputed. Divide booked or used hours by capacity hours for the period you need. From June to August the two LC-MS/MS systems were booked for 91% and used for 84% of capacity, up from 74% booked and 67% used from March to May. The other 18 bookable instruments were used for 48% of capacity from June to August.
Recorded downtime across the 20 bookable instruments was 265 hours from March to August, including 58 hours on INS-002 in July for an ion-source repair spread over two weeks.

Preventive maintenance intervals are 6 or 12 months by instrument type. Maintenance dates are copied from the Lab Operations spreadsheet and vendor portals, which remain the records of maintenance and calibration.

Loblolly Ridge Therapeutics • 0.9 (for review)
Design Proposal: Bioanalytical 
LC-MS/MS Capacity
Loblolly Ridge Therapeutics | DMPK & Bioanalytical with Lab Operations | 
2026-09-15 | v0.9 (for review)
Draft for review. This proposal sets out how DMPK & Bioanalytical and Lab Operations 
could meet discovery and development bioanalytical demand in 2027. It compares three 
options: a second LC-MS/MS triple-quadrupole system, a second shift on the existing 
systems, or sending more discovery bioanalysis to external laboratories. It does not 
recommend an option yet; research leadership expects to decide on October 2, 2026.
1. Why this is needed now
The two in-house LC-MS/MS triple-quadrupole systems ran close to their practical limit this 
summer, and discovery samples have been moving to external laboratories to keep projects 
moving. Turnaround is much longer externally, and 2027 will bring more work. An 
instrument ordered after October would not be in routine use before the second quarter of 
2027, so the choice has to be made this autumn.
2. Evidence: instrument use
From June to August 2026 the two LC-MS/MS systems were booked for 91% and used for 
84% of their capacity hours, up from 74% booked and 67% used from March to May. The 
other 18 bookable instruments were used for 48% of capacity. Each LC-MS/MS system has 
about 100 available hours a week including the unattended overnight queue, so there is no 
idle time left to schedule into.
Recorded downtime across the 20 bookable instruments was 265 hours from March to 
August, including 58 hours on INS-002 in July for an ion-source repair. With two systems, 
one outage halves capacity. The chart shows used hours by month for all 20 bookable 
instruments.

discovery studies, with receipt, analysis and data-transfer dates as of September 18, 2026. 
Sample counts only; no subject identifiers.
4. Demand in 2027
Bioanalytical demand will rise with DP-07 candidate profiling, LRT-4051 metabolite work 
and pharmacokinetic sampling in CANOPY-OLE. The CANOPY-OLE sampling volume is an 
assumption the clinical team has not yet confirmed. Clinical samples are analyzed 
externally, because the Woodlands laboratory is non-GxP, but they draw on the same 
external capacity that takes our discovery overflow.
5. Requirements
 Discovery pharmacokinetic results within about a week of sampling, so that design 
cycles are not held up.
 Enough headroom that one instrument outage does not stop discovery bioanalysis.
 Results that arrive in the assay registry and data hub without extra manual handling. 
External results arrive as transfer files; the proposed Data Hub phase 2 would automate 
their intake but is not approved.
 No change to where GLP and clinical bioanalysis is done.
6. Options
 A. Second triple-quadrupole system: about $640,000 capital and six to eight months to 
routine use, including installation, method transfer and qualification. Adds about 100 
hours a week once running.
 B. Second shift on the existing systems: one additional scientist to run attended evening 
work and method development. Lower cost, faster to start, but no protection against an 
instrument outage. Staffing cost not yet estimated.
 C. More external discovery bioanalysis: about $30,000 a month at current volume, using 
Alder and, once qualified, Fenwick. No capital, but turnaround stays near three weeks.
7. Trade-offs
Option A costs most up front and takes longest, but it is the only option that restores in-
house turnaround at higher volume and adds resilience. Option B could start within a 
quarter but depends on hiring and does not help when an instrument is down. Option C is 
flexible and needs no capital, but it keeps discovery waiting about 22 days for results and 
competes with CANOPY-OLE and LRT-4051 work at the same laboratories. Options can be 
combined; B or C could bridge until A is running.
Loblolly Ridge Therapeutics • 0.9 (for review)
8. Open decision and information needed
 Decision owner: research leadership, on October 2, 2026.
 CANOPY-OLE sampling volume, to be confirmed by the clinical team.
 Cost of a second shift, to be estimated with People and Finance.
 Fenwick qualification timing, from QA.
 Vendor quotes for option A, held by DMPK & Bioanalytical and not attached to this draft.

files.title: Assay Data Review and Release Work Instruction
files.filename: Assay Data Review and Release Work Instruction.pdf
files.search:
Assay Data Review and Release Work Instruction
Loblolly Ridge Therapeutics | Discovery Biology | 2025-10-20
Work instruction WI-DB-007, revision B. It describes how an in vitro assay run is completed,
checked, uploaded, reviewed and released, from the instrument to the assay registry and the R&D
Data Hub. It applies to all Discovery Biology and DMPK assay runs at the Woodlands laboratory.
1. Purpose and principles
Assay results drive compound design and project decisions, so every released result must be
traceable to its run, its raw data and the people who produced and reviewed it. Research at the
Woodlands laboratory is non-GxP, but we apply attributable, contemporaneous and reviewed
record-keeping as good practice. FDA describes data integrity as the completeness, consistency
and accuracy of data; audit trails in the ELN and the registry let changes be reconstructed.
2. Where the data go
Results flow from the instrument and chromatography data system into the ELN experiment, then to
the assay registry, and nightly into the R&D Data Hub, where they are joined to compound
identifiers from the compound database. Only released results reach the Data Hub dashboards.
3. Roles
Scientist: runs the assay, records the ELN entry, applies acceptance criteria and uploads the run.
Reviewer: a second qualified scientist who did not perform the run; signs off or returns it.
Research Informatics: maintains the registry and reviews correction requests.
4. Steps
4.1 Complete the run and the ELN entry on the same or the next working day. Attach the instrument
export and plate map, and record reagent lots and deviations from the method.
4.2 Apply the acceptance criteria for the assay (controls, reference compound, plate statistics).
Criteria for each assay are in its method record.
4.3 If the run fails, record why. Repeat the plates when material allows and record the outcome as
fail-repeat, or record fail-invalid if the run cannot be repeated.
4.4 Export the run from the ELN and import it into the assay registry. This is a manual step done by
the scientist; check that the plate count and compound IDs match the ELN entry.
4.5 Request review in the registry. The reviewer checks the raw data, the calculation and the
acceptance criteria, then signs off or returns the run with comments.

4.6 On sign-off, release the run. If a run is invalidated, choose a reason code from the registry pick
list and add a comment.
5. Corrections after release
A released result cannot be edited. To correct it, submit a registry correction request with the
reason and the evidence; Research Informatics reviews it and the reviewer of the original run
confirms the change. The registry keeps the original and corrected values.
6. Timeliness
Aim to upload a run within two working days of the ELN entry and to complete review within three
working days of the request. Project teams read the Data Hub dashboards each morning, so an
unreleased run is invisible to them.
7. Revision history
Rev. B, October 2025 – fail-repeat and fail-invalid outcomes defined; reviewer independence
stated; correction requests routed to Research Informatics.
Rev. A, March 2025 – first issue with R&D Data Hub phase 1.

files.title: Research Data Flow Architecture Note
files.search:
Loblolly Ridge Therapeutics • 1.2
Research Data Flow Architecture Note
Loblolly Ridge Therapeutics | Research Informatics | 2026-09-02 | v1.2
This note describes how research data move at Loblolly Ridge: from laboratory instruments 
and the electronic lab notebook through the assay registry and compound database to the 
R&D Data Hub, and how data from external partners arrive. It names the components, the 
flows between them, when each flow runs, who owns it, what happens when it fails and the 
known gaps. Version 1.2 adds measured upload lag for 2026.
1. System boundary
In scope: research data generated in the Woodlands laboratory and research data received 
from external partners. Out of scope: CRO-hosted clinical systems (EDC, CTMS, eTMF), the 
safety database and finance systems, which have their own owners. Discovery research is 
non-GxP; the note describes good-practice controls, not validated GxP systems.
2. Components
 Instrument data server and chromatography data system: acquisition and processing 
for the LC-MS/MS and LC instruments.
 Electronic lab notebook: cloud ELN, in use since 2020; the record of each experiment.
 Assay and sample registry: internal lightweight LIMS built in 2021; the record of 
released assay results and registered samples.
 Compound registration database: legacy system from 2014; the source of compound 
identifiers and structures.
 R&D Data Hub: research data warehouse and dashboards; phase 1 live since March 
2025 with nightly loads from the registry and compound database.
 Infrastructure: servers, backup and network are run by Bayou Managed IT under our IT 
team's direction.
3. Data flows
Assay results flow from instruments and the chromatography data system into ELN 
experiments, then to the assay registry, and nightly into the R&D Data Hub, where they are 
joined to compound identifiers from the compound database. The diagram shows the four 
internal flows.
Loblolly Ridge Therapeutics • 1.2
4. Interfaces and timing
 Instrument to ELN: the scientist attaches the processed export to the ELN experiment.
 ELN to registry: manual export and import by the scientist after the run passes 
acceptance criteria.
 Registry to Data Hub: automated nightly load of released runs.
 Compound database to Data Hub: automated nightly load of compound identifiers.
 External partners: scheduled transfers arrive as files – EDC extracts from the CRO 
monthly and blinded, central lab results, IRT extracts weekly, ambulatory blood-
pressure data monthly and bioanalytical results per batch. These are checked by 
Biometrics or DMPK and are not loaded into the Data Hub.
5. Measured lag, January to August 2026
For 1,450 assay runs, the median time from run to registry upload was 4 days, with a 90th 
percentile of 11 days. DP-09 runs took a median of 7 days, other projects 4. 1,305 runs 
passed acceptance criteria, 103 failed and were repeated, and 42 were invalidated. The 
chart shows plates run by month.
Loblolly Ridge Therapeutics • 1.2
Measure Value
Measure plates
Unit plates
Total 4812
Mean 3.3186
Records 1450
Period 2026-01-01 to 2026-08-31
In vitro assay runs registered January to August 2026, with ELN entry, registry upload and 
reviewer sign-off dates as of September 18, 2026.
6. Responsibilities
 Research Informatics: registry, Data Hub, nightly loads, correction requests.
 Discovery Biology and DMPK: ELN entries, uploads and reviews, following the assay 
data review and release work instruction.
 IT with Bayou Managed IT: infrastructure, access and backup.
 Data owners in each function: fitness of their data for decisions.
7. Failure and correction handling
If a nightly load fails, Research Informatics reruns it the next morning and posts a notice on 
the Data Hub home page. Released registry results are corrected only through a registry 
correction request, which keeps the original value; the ELN and registry audit trails let 
changes be reconstructed, in line with FDA's description of audit trails as secure, time-
stamped records of changes to electronic records.
8. Known gaps
 The ELN-to-registry step is manual and accounts for most upload lag.
 External bioanalytical and CRO transfers are not loaded into the Data Hub, so project 
teams see them only in files.
Loblolly Ridge Therapeutics • 1.2
 When a hosted system or partner contract ends, the data and linked metadata must be 
obtained and kept; FDA guidance makes the same point. We have no written exit 
checklist for research systems yet.
 The compound registration database dates from 2014; an upgrade is under discussion.
 The proposed Data Hub phase 2 would add direct ELN-to-registry transfer and intake of 
external bioanalytical and CRO transfers. It is a proposal and has not been approved or 
budgeted.

files.filename: CRO and Laboratory Data Transfer Specification.docx
files.search:
Loblolly Ridge Therapeutics • 1.4
CRO and Laboratory Data Transfer 
Specification
Loblolly Ridge Therapeutics | Biometrics with Research Informatics | 2026-
05-20 | v1.4
Data transfer specification DTS-C1-001, version 1.4. It defines the scheduled data transfers 
from external partners to Loblolly Ridge for CANOPY-1 and CANOPY-OLE: who sends what, 
how often, how files are named and versioned, what is checked on receipt and how errors 
are handled. Owner: Biometrics, with Research Informatics. Shared with Halvorsen Clinical 
Research data management, Meridian Central Laboratories and Alder Bioanalytical.
1. Producers and consumers
Halvorsen Clinical Research is the full-service CRO for CANOPY-1 and, under a separate 
work order effective April 20, 2026, for CANOPY-OLE. It hosts the EDC and sends blinded 
EDC extracts. Meridian Central Laboratories loads central lab results into the CRO systems 
and sends them to Loblolly Ridge. Cobalt RTSM sends IRT extracts. Pulsewell ABPM Services 
sends ambulatory blood-pressure data. Alder Bioanalytical sends pharmacokinetic sample 
results.
Biometrics receives all transfers into the controlled transfer area; DMPK & Bioanalytical 
also reviews bioanalytical results. The diagram shows the main routes.

Loblolly Ridge Therapeutics • 1.4
2. Record types
 EDC extract: all CRF datasets at dataset level, blinded; no treatment assignment 
variables.
 Central lab: results with specimen, visit, test code, units and reference ranges.
 IRT: randomization and dispensing events without treatment codes, plus depot and site 
inventory.
 ABPM: session-level summary records and device identifiers.
 Bioanalytical: sample-level concentration results with batch identifiers and assay run 
references.
3. Schedule
Scheduled transfers: EDC extracts from the CRO monthly (blinded); central lab results every 
two weeks; IRT extracts weekly; ambulatory blood-pressure data monthly; bioanalytical 
results per batch. Transfer specification version 1.4 sets the two-week central lab schedule.
4. File naming and versioning
Files are named study, source, data type, cut date and version, for example C1-MCL-
LAB-20260515-v1.zip. A resent file for the same cut increments the version. Every transfer 
includes a transmittal listing file names, record counts per dataset and the cut date. 
Superseded versions are kept, not overwritten.
5. Checks on receipt
Each transfer is checked on receipt for file naming, version, record counts against the 
transmittal, required fields, and study and visit identifiers. Discrepancies are logged and 
resolved with the sender before loading. Checks and outcomes are recorded in the transfer 
log.
6. Error handling
 Naming or version error: sender resends with the next version.
 Record count mismatch: transfer held; sender confirms counts or resends within two 
business days.
 Missing required field or unknown visit: transfer held; discrepancy raised with the 
sender's data manager.
 Repeated failures from the same sender are raised at the joint operations committee.
7. Retention and system exit
Loblolly Ridge keeps every received file and transmittal for the life of the study archive.
Loblolly Ridge Therapeutics • 1.4
FDA guidance says that when hosted systems are decommissioned or contracts end, 
sponsors should obtain and retain metadata linked to the data; at database lock and at 
contract end the CRO will provide final extracts with audit trails and metadata. FDA 
describes data integrity as the completeness, consistency and accuracy of data, which these 
checks are designed to protect.
8. Example transmittal
 Study: CANOPY-1. Source: Meridian Central Laboratories. Cut date: 2026-05-15. 
Version: 1.
 Files: C1-MCL-LAB-20260515-v1.zip (results), C1-MCL-REF-20260515-v1.csv 
(reference ranges).

Clinical Supply Chain and CDMO Network
 Overview
Loblolly Ridge Therapeutics | CMC & Clinical Supply | 2026-08-10
How clinical and development supply moves through Loblolly Ridge's outsourced manufacturing
network: from the API manufacturers to drug-product manufacture, packaging, depots and sites,
and to our licensee. It explains who does what at each node, how forecasts and campaigns are
planned, how material is released, how safety stock is held and where the backup API supplier
project stands. Issued August 10, 2026.
Network map
LRT-1107 API is made by Tessaro Fine Chemicals in Italy and drug product by Northgate Pharma
Services in Ontario. Clearwing Clinical Supply packages, labels and distributes to depots in the
United States and the Netherlands, which supply CANOPY-1 and CANOPY-OLE sites. The
diagram also shows Hanlin Pharmatech as a second API source; Hanlin is in qualification and is not
yet approved to supply.
Roles by node
Tessaro Fine Chemicals (API CDMO, Italy): LRT-1107 API; LRT-3318 drug substance for our
licensee; GMP API for LRT-4051.
Northgate Pharma Services (drug-product CDMO, Canada): LRT-1107 drug product; LRT-4051
clinical drug product.
Clearwing Clinical Supply: packaging, labelling, depots and distribution to sites.

Brookmoor Analytical: analytical methods and stability testing, including for LRT-4051.
Cobalt RTSM (IRT): randomization and dispensing data that drive resupply.
CMC & Clinical Supply: forecasting, campaign planning and partner management. Quality
Assurance: release.
Forecasting and campaign planning
CMC & Clinical Supply refreshes the LRT-1107 clinical supply forecast monthly from IRT
randomization and dispensing data and plans API and drug-product campaigns 12 to 18 months
ahead of need. The forecast covers both CANOPY-1 and CANOPY-OLE, and is reviewed with
Clinical Operations when the enrollment forecast changes.
Release and quality
Quality Assurance releases each drug-product lot for clinical use after reviewing the executed batch
record and certificate of analysis, and releases packaged and labelled kits before they ship to
depots. Quality agreements with each CDMO set out who is responsible for what under CGMP;
FDA guidance describes a quality agreement as separate from commercial terms such as price. All
manufacturing, testing and supply partners are risk tier 1 and are audited before first use and every
24 months.
Safety stock
Loblolly Ridge keeps at least six months of forecast LRT-1107 drug-product demand as safety
stock across the U.S. and EU depots. No site has run out of study drug.
Supply to our licensee
Castellane Pharma runs development of LRT-3318. Until technology transfer to Castellane's
manufacturer completes, targeted for March 2027, we supply drug substance at a transfer price.
Deliveries in 2026 were 6.0 kg on February 24 and 8.5 kg on June 23; the next, 8.5 kg, is scheduled
for November 20.
Backup API supplier
Tessaro is the only qualified API source for LRT-1107. Hanlin Pharmatech in China is being
qualified as a backup. Its qualification audit took place on June 9, 2026; acceptance of the audit
response is planned for mid-August and the qualification batch for December 2026. Hanlin will not
supply clinical material until QA approves it.

files.title: Quality Management System Overview
files.search:
Quality Management System Overview
Loblolly Ridge Therapeutics | Quality Assurance | 2026-02-02
An overview of the Loblolly Ridge quality management system: what it covers, where GxP rules
apply to our work, how controlled documents are organized, the core quality processes, who is
responsible and how management reviews the system. Revision 5 reflects the move to the eQMS in
November 2025. The detailed requirements are in the SOPs listed in the eQMS.
Scope
The quality management system covers GCP, GLP oversight, GMP oversight and
pharmacovigilance activities performed or sponsored by Loblolly Ridge, and computerized-system
validation for GxP systems. Discovery research is outside GxP scope.
Where GxP applies to our work
Clinical studies are run under GCP. We are the sponsor; our CRO and other service providers
perform transferred activities under our oversight. Nonclinical safety studies that support regulatory
submissions are done under GLP at qualified external testing facilities, each with a quality
assurance unit independent of the study staff; we oversee them but do not run a GLP facility.
Manufacturing and testing of clinical material are done under GMP at CDMOs and contract
laboratories; our QA releases material for clinical use.
Pharmacovigilance is GxP work shared with our safety database provider. GxP computerized
systems, including the eQMS, are validated. Research at the Woodlands laboratory is non-GxP, but
research records are kept attributable, contemporaneous and reviewed as good practice.
Outsourced activities
Most GxP work is done by partners. ICH Q10 makes the company responsible for controlling
outsourced activities, including assessing suppliers before use, written agreements and monitoring
performance. Partners are risk-tiered: tier 1 partners, the GxP-critical ones, are audited before first
use and every 24 months; tier 2 every 36 months or by questionnaire; tier 3 have no routine audit.
The 2026 audit program covers tier 1 partners due for routine audit, for-cause audits and an internal
audit of TMF oversight.
Document hierarchy
Controlled documents run from policies to SOPs, work instructions, and forms and templates. SOPs
and policies are reviewed every 24 months; forms and research work instructions every 36 months.
Since November 17, 2025 all controlled documents, training records, deviations and CAPA are
managed in the eQMS, which replaced a controlled file share and paper training records.
Core quality processes
Document control and periodic review.

Training: role-based curricula assigned and recorded in the eQMS.
Deviations, audit findings and supplier notifications, classified minor, major or critical. A CAPA is
required for major and critical events and for repeated minor ones; effectiveness checks follow
CAPA closure.
Change control for GxP processes and systems.
Partner qualification, audits and oversight.
Data integrity: FDA defines data integrity as the completeness, consistency and accuracy of data;
our GxP systems keep secure, time-stamped audit trails.
Release of clinical material.
Roles
Head of Quality: owns the quality management system and reports on it to the CEO.
QA GCP and pharmacovigilance lead: clinical and safety oversight audits.
QA GMP lead: CDMO oversight and material release.
QA GLP oversight: deputy role to be assigned; covered by the Head of Quality in the meantime.
Function heads: follow the procedures that apply to their teams and own their controlled
documents.
Management review
Quality Assurance holds an annual management review each February, chaired by the CEO with
the executive team, covering audits, quality events and CAPA, training, document control, partner
quality and resources. The review sets the quality objectives for the year and records decisions and
resource needs.

files.title: eQMS Migration Post-Implementation Review
files.search:
Loblolly Ridge Therapeutics • 1.0
eQMS Migration Post-Implementation 
Review
Loblolly Ridge Therapeutics | Quality Assurance with IT | 2025-12-12 | v1.0
Post-implementation review of the eQMS migration, which moved document control, 
training records and CAPA from a controlled file share and paper records into a cloud eQMS. 
The system went live on November 17, 2025. This review compares objectives with 
outcomes, lists what is still open and records lessons for future system projects.
Objectives
The project set out to bring document control, training records and CAPA into one validated 
system with electronic signatures and audit trails, and to retire the controlled file share and 
paper training records. It covered all GxP areas in the quality management system: GCP, GLP 
oversight, GMP oversight, pharmacovigilance and computerized-system validation.
What was delivered
 Document control in the eQMS for all controlled documents, with the hierarchy of 
policies, SOPs, work instructions, and forms and templates, and review cycles of 24 
months for SOPs and policies and 36 months for forms and research work instructions.
 Training records and role-based curricula for employees.
 Deviations, audit findings and CAPA in one workflow.
 Validation of the configured system, completed before go-live on November 17, 2025.
Measures at go-live
199 controlled documents were migrated into the eQMS, each with its existing effective 
date. To keep document content stable during migration, a freeze ran from August to 
November 2025 and periodic reviews were deferred. As a result, a group of migrated 
documents will pass their review due dates during 2026.
Residual items and owners
 Training-matrix mapping for long-term contractors – People, with QA. Contractors are 
still trained from paper lists.
 Retiring the legacy file share – IT, once read-only access is no longer needed for 
reference.
 Loading historical CAPA records closed before go-live – QA.
Loblolly Ridge Therapeutics • 1.0
Lessons
 Keeping effective dates on migration was right for traceability, but it moved the review 
due dates with it. Future migrations should schedule the review backlog before the 
freeze starts.
 The four-month freeze was longer than planned because validation testing started late. 
Validation resources should be booked when the vendor is selected.
 Contractor records need their own mapping; they do not follow employee role 
structures.
 Early training of document owners reduced support requests in the first weeks.
Closure recommendation
The eQMS is in routine use and the project objectives have been met except for the three 
residual items. We recommend closing the project and tracking the residual items as actions 
in the eQMS, reviewed at the February 2026 management review.

2025 Quality Management Review Summary
Loblolly Ridge Therapeutics | Quality Assurance | 2026-02-20
Summary of the 2025 quality management review, held in February 2026 and chaired by the CEO
with the executive team. It records the 2025 inputs, the measures reviewed, the decisions taken
and the quality objectives for 2026.
Inputs reviewed
Partner and internal audits.
Quality events and CAPA.
Training.
Document control and the eQMS migration.
Partner quality and resources.
2025 measures
Quality events: 72 were opened in 2025, 6 of them major and none critical; 69 were closed by year
end, with a median time to close of 39 days. By source: internal lab 23, vendor audit 17, document
control 9, CDMO batch 9, CRO or site via the CRO 8, and supplier 6. Events are classified minor,
major or critical; a CAPA is required for major and critical events and for repeated minor ones.
Audits: Quality Assurance completed 10 partner audits and one internal audit of document control.
The partner audits produced 17 findings, each logged as a quality event.
Training: on-time completion of assigned training was 93%; most late items fell in November and
December, when training records moved into the eQMS.
Documents: the eQMS went live on November 17, 2025. Periodic reviews were deferred during the
August to November migration freeze, so a group of migrated documents will pass their review due
dates in 2026.
Decisions and 2026 objectives
The review set three quality objectives for 2026: clear the periodic-review backlog by June 30,
2026; complete the tier 1 audit program; and qualify a backup API supplier. The 2026 audit program
covers tier 1 partners due for routine audit, for-cause audits and an internal audit of TMF oversight;
upcoming routine audits include Alder Bioanalytical, Aster Archive Services and Northgate Pharma
Services in the autumn.
Resource needs
Document owner time in the first half of 2026 to clear the periodic-review backlog.

External auditor support for tier 1 audits outside the United States.
A GLP oversight deputy in QA.
Training-matrix mapping for contractors, with People.

Loblolly Ridge Therapeutics Company Overview
Loblolly Ridge Therapeutics | Business Development with Corporate Communications | 2026-07-15
Loblolly Ridge Therapeutics is a clinical-stage company in The Woodlands, Texas, developing oral
small-molecule medicines for serious chronic cardiometabolic, renal and neuropathic-pain
conditions. All of our product candidates are investigational and none is approved for any use.
What we do
We discover and develop oral small-molecule medicines. Our work runs from target validation and
medicinal chemistry through clinical development and regulatory submissions. We have no
marketed products and no commercial organization; our focus is on taking programs through
development and working with partners where they can take a program further.
Portfolio at a glance
LRT-1107 – in Phase 3 for treatment-resistant hypertension.
LRT-2240 – has completed Phase 2a in chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy.
LRT-3318 – licensed to Castellane Pharma for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis
(MASH).
LRT-4051 – in IND-enabling studies for diabetic kidney disease.
Discovery programs in cardiometabolic, renal and neuropathic-pain biology.
All are investigational.
How we work
We combine in-house discovery biology, DMPK, clinical development, regulatory and quality teams
with a qualified network of clinical, nonclinical and manufacturing partners. Our teams design the
science, own the development plans and oversee the partners who run studies and make clinical
supplies.
Where we are
Loblolly Ridge Therapeutics, Inc. is a privately held Delaware corporation founded in 2012 and
headquartered in The Woodlands, Texas, where our offices and research laboratory are located.
We have about 125 employees.
Partnering interests
We are seeking partners for LRT-2240 (global or regional), for ex-U.S. rights to LRT-1107, and for
research collaborations around our cardiometabolic discovery work.

Contact
Business Development, Loblolly Ridge Therapeutics, Inc., The Woodlands, Texas. Partnering
discussions beyond this overview take place under a confidentiality agreement.

Decisions requested
 Approve CANOPY-1 change order 4: $3.72 million in CRO services plus an estimated 
$2.38 million in pass-through costs. Board approval is required because the total 
including pass-through is $5 million or more.
 Agree the first quarter of 2027 as the decision point for LRT-2240: partner, self-fund a 
Phase 2b start, or hold.
 Note that research leadership will decide on bioanalytical capacity on October 2, within 
management's approval limits, and will report the outcome at this meeting.
 Agree to take the financing timing decision in the first quarter of 2027.
Business context
Our value over the next year rests on CANOPY-1. The study had randomized 467 of 640 
participants (73%) at 104 of 112 sites by August 31. Topline results are now forecast for 
September 14, 2027, against July 2, 2027 in the FY2026 plan. LRT-4051 is on course for an 
IND in June 2027, about five weeks later than the April 30 baseline, because toxicology 
reports and GMP API release have moved into December.
Cash and investments were $231 million on June 30, 2026, after the $185 million Series D in 
March 2025. Of the venture debt facility of up to $60 million, $25 million is drawn. At the 
approved FY2026 plan and current commitments, management estimates cash runway into 
the second half of 2028, before any new partnering income. We have received $55 million 
from Castellane for LRT-3318 and are eligible for up to $590 million in further milestones 
plus tiered royalties.
Evidence: the September reforecast
January to August R&D was $59.5 million against a $64.4 million phased budget, $4.9 
million under, mainly from timing in nonclinical and CMC work.
Loblolly Ridge Therapeutics • 1.0
The September reforecast puts FY2026 R&D at $95.07 million against the $94.8 million 
budget, $0.27 million over, after releasing $1.25 million of the reserve. LRT-1107 is forecast 
at $55.05 million against $52.60 million, including the first months of change order 4. The 
table summarizes the reforecast across the 56 budget cells.

Change order 4
What it buys. One additional country with six planned sites, and about three more months 
of CRO services to cover the longer enrollment period. The current forecast for last 
participant randomized, March 16, 2027, assumes the added country opens as planned.
What it costs. $3.72 million in services and an estimated $2.38 million in pass-through. 
About $1.3 million falls in FY2026, already in the reforecast; the rest falls in 2027 and early 
2028.
Loblolly Ridge Therapeutics • 1.0
Signed Halvorsen commitments for CANOPY-1 already total $64.16 million in services, 
including change orders 1 to 3 at $4.73 million.
If we do not approve it. Enrollment continues in the existing 11 countries at the recent rate, 
which management expects would push last participant randomized toward the later end of 
the January to May 2027 range the CRO presented in June, and delay topline accordingly.
Management recommends approval.
LRT-2240: the path if no partner commits
The partnering tracker has 18 conversations for LRT-2240: 12 confidentiality agreements, 6 
data-room accesses and 2 companies at management-meeting stage. No term sheet had 
been received by September 18, and indicative proposals are now expected in January 2027 
rather than October.
Phase 2b readiness was paused in July. If no partner commits by the first quarter of 2027, 
the choices are to self-fund a Phase 2b start, to keep partnering without starting Phase 2b, 
or to hold the program. A Phase 2b start would trigger a $5 million milestone to Tamsin 
Biosciences, within total obligations of up to $28 million in milestones and low-single-digit 
royalties. We will bring a costed recommendation to the first board meeting of 2027.
Bioanalytical capacity
Research leadership will choose between a second LC-MS/MS triple-quadrupole system 
(about $640,000 capital and six to eight months to routine use), a second shift on the 
existing systems (one additional scientist) and sending more discovery bioanalysis to 
external laboratories (about $30,000 a month at current volume). The choice is within 
management's authority; it is included because it affects 2027 spend and the pace of DP-07 
and LRT-4051 work.
Financing timing
Management plans to decide in the first quarter of 2027 whether to raise additional capital 
before or after CANOPY-1 topline results. Raising before topline protects the balance sheet 
against a later readout; raising after topline could be on better terms if the results support 
the program. Investor approaches and valuation will be discussed in the meeting and are 
not in this paper.
Portfolio risk in one view
The PMO register holds 150 milestones: 100 complete, 20 on track, 21 at risk, 4 late and 5 
not started. The late items are CANOPY-1 site activation and the 75% randomization 
milestone, acceptance of the backup API supplier's audit response and the periodic-review 
backlog in Quality.
Loblolly Ridge Therapeutics • 1.0
Five of seven LRT-3318 technology-transfer packages had been accepted by September 14.
Requested action
Approve change order 4 as set out above, and agree that the LRT-2240 path and financing 
timing will come back to the board in the first quarter of 2027 with recommendations.

Information Package Cover Memo
Loblolly Ridge Therapeutics | Portfolio & Program Management | 2026-09-25  
| v1.0
To the advisory team, from Grace Okafor, Vice President, Portfolio & Program Management. 
This memo accompanies the information package for your review of how Loblolly Ridge 
coordinates R&D programs, external partners, laboratory and development information, 
and budgets ahead of the 2027 readouts and financing decisions.
Purpose of the package
Loblolly Ridge Therapeutics, Inc. is a privately held company founded in 2012 and 
headquartered in The Woodlands, Texas, with 128 employees on September 1, 2026. We 
engaged your team in September 2026. The package contains selected documents, registers 
and extracts that show how we work today. It is not a complete record, and each document 
states its own date and version.
Contents by area
 Company and portfolio: Loblolly Ridge Therapeutics Company Overview (July 2026); 
Corporate Partnering Overview; Development Portfolio Summary – September 2026; 
Portfolio Project and Milestone Register; Board Executive Brief: Capital Allocation 
Ahead of 2027 Readouts.
 Governance and resourcing: Stage-Gate and Portfolio Governance Procedure (rev. 3.1); 
FY2026 R&D Resource Allocation Workbook.
 Budgets: FY2026 R&D Budget, Forecast and Accruals Workbook; Monthly R&D Accrual 
Close Procedure (v2.0); R&D Budget Review After August Close.
 Outsourcing: External Partner Register and Work Orders; External Partner Selection, 
Qualification and Oversight SOP (rev. 4.0); Work Order and Change Order Process 
(v1.3); Vendor Deliverables Tracker, January–August 2026; External Partner 
Performance Review – Q3 2026 Interim.
 LRT-1107: CANOPY-1 CRO Oversight Plan (v2.1); CANOPY-1 Enrollment Forecast 
Working Session with Halvorsen (June); CANOPY-1 Program Team Checkpoint – 
September 2026; LRT-1107 Development Program Overview (v3.0).
 LRT-2240: LRT-2240 Non-Confidential Partnering Presentation; LRT-2240 Virtual Data 
Room Index; LRT-2240 Partnering Opportunity Tracker.
 LRT-3318: LRT-3318 Technology Transfer Status Note.
 LRT-4051: LRT-4051 IND-Enabling Workplan; LRT-4051 IND-Enabling Development 
Plan (v1.3); LRT-4051 Phase 1 Outsourcing Options.
Loblolly Ridge Therapeutics • 1.0
 Laboratory: Research Laboratory Operations Guide (rev. C); Laboratory Instrument 
Register and Utilization, March–August 2026; Design Proposal: Bioanalytical LC-MS/MS 
Capacity (draft 0.9); Research Leadership Review: Bioanalytical Capacity Options.
 Research data: Assay Data Review and Release Work Instruction (rev. B); Research Data 
Flow Architecture Note (v1.2); R&D Data Hub Phase 2 Proposal Review; CRO and 
Laboratory Data Transfer Specification (v1.4).
 Supply: Clinical Supply Chain and CDMO Network Overview.
 Quality: Quality Management System Overview (rev. 5); eQMS Migration Post-
Implementation Review; 2025 Quality Management Review Summary; Controlled 
Documents and Quality Events Workbook.
What is not included
The package excludes full contracts, CRO-hosted patient-level systems, board minutes and 
partner-confidential terms. We have also not included the CRO enrollment extract by site, 
the monthly CANOPY-1 joint operations committee minutes, the Castellane obligations 
tracker, the LRT-2240 steering deck, the bioanalytical capital request memo or the Q4 2026 
FTE plan, which is still in draft. Some documents refer to these; ask us if you need to see one 
and we will tell you whether it can be shared.
Data conventions
 Our fiscal year is the calendar year. Amounts are in U.S. dollars.
 Dates are as stated in each document; registers are extracts as of the date shown and 
later events are not reflected.
 Workbooks include a Read me, a Summary of formula totals, a Dictionary and the data 
sheets. Some Summary totals are not meaningful measures, and the Read me says 
which.
 FTE figures are planning estimates by function heads, not timesheet data.
 All Loblolly Ridge product candidates are investigational. Nothing in the package 
describes clinical results.
Contacts
 Package coordination and portfolio: Grace Okafor, Portfolio & Program Management.
 Budgets and accruals: Janelle Whitaker, Controller, for Dev Raghunathan, CFO.
 Outsourcing and partner register: Kendra Mbatha, Outsourcing & Procurement.
 Clinical operations: Luis Ybarra.
 Quality: Dr. Anneliese Park.
 Laboratory and research data: Beth Kowalczyk and Samuel Oyelaran.
 Please route requests for additional documents through Portfolio & Program 
Management.
